why: One CI guard and its own self-test: scripts/ci/check_register_field_loss.py's FINDINGS stop asserting a cause the code does not establish ('the write-back somebody else made, reverted silently'), state what was measured and what was not, carry the behind-base caveat per finding rather than only in the summary, and branch the FIX line to lead with `git merge origin/main` where that is the actual remedy. Plus one backlog row resolved. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path, no live-VM mutation, no secret, and nothing in LANDING_MACHINERY. The guard's DECISIONS are unchanged -- base_state alters only what a finding SAYS, and a self-test control asserts that the same findings fire either way, so this cannot silence anything. Evidence is planted-defect: six mutations each shown to land (pattern count asserted) and each shown to fail --self-test, control quiet. TWO OF THE FIRST FIVE ESCAPED and were fixed in the tests rather than worked around: cutting base_state from the live compare() call left the suite green because every control called the pure function directly (now covered by a LIVE control over an unrelated history), and deleting the FIX branch escaped because the assertion was satisfied by the findings' own caveat text (the lead string is now a module constant render itself emits). Live --base origin/main OK, ruff clean, and the full guard set is 77 pass / 1 fail where the one failure is this guard pre-arming.
